## UNFI Deductions and Disputes: A CPG Brand's Guide (2026)


*The UNFI policies in this guide — payment terms, the Simplified Supplier Approach and its 2.5% fee, the five scorecard thresholds, compliance-fee categories, spoils and reclamation rules, and the 12-month dispute window — are drawn directly from UNFI's official Supplier Policies & Guidelines, the policy document UNFI issues to its suppliers.*


Your UNFI remittance showing up short is a solvable problem. Understanding why it happens, knowing which charges you can push back on, and having a process that doesn't fall apart on small-dollar claims — that's the part most suppliers are still figuring out. This guide covers how UNFI deductions are structured, what the Simplified Supplier Approach changes about your fee exposure, and how to build a dispute and prevention workflow that holds up.


**TL;DR:**


- Most UNFI shortage claims that get written off are disputable; brands skip them because manual review costs more in staff time than the individual recovery is worth
- You have 12 months to dispute any UNFI deduction, and the clock starts when UNFI records it — not when you spot it on a remittance
- The Simplified Supplier Approach charges a 2.5% fee on total purchases and waives compliance fees when you clear all five monthly scorecard thresholds
- [Glimpse automates UNFI dispute filing](https://www.tryglimpse.com/deductions-management) and cash application with no minimum dollar threshold and setup in 45 days or fewer


## What Are UNFI Deductions and Why Do They Hit CPG Brands Hard?


UNFI pays suppliers net of deductions: every remittance reflects the invoice total minus fees, allowances, and chargebacks that UNFI subtracts before the check is cut. The supplier receives a check that's short, plus a list of codes to decode. Any amount UNFI can't deduct within 30 days of its due date gets billed to the supplier directly and is due immediately.


In Glimpse's experience working with hundreds of CPG brands, most deductions that flow through are disputable, and most never get disputed. The gap isn't that brands are making the most mistakes — it's that they aren't tracking or challenging closely enough to catch what's invalid before the window closes.


### What Are the Main UNFI Deduction Categories?


UNFI remittances carry six recurring charge types, and knowing which category a line item falls into tells you whether it's disputable and where to look in the Supplier Policies.


Deduction Type What Triggers It Typically Disputable?


Shortages UNFI's DC count comes in below the PO quantity Yes, with signed BOL


MCBs / Promotional Allowances Customer discounts passed through to supplier Depends on agreement


Pricing / Cost Discrepancies Invoice price doesn't match PO price Yes, with documentation


Spoils / Damages Products damaged or expired inside a DC Partially


Compliance Fees Appointment, load, fill rate, or label violations Yes, if threshold was met


Reclamations / Resets Retailer pass-through credits and reset labor costs Rarely


Shortages are the highest-volume dispute category. UNFI's case count at the DC governs payment, so if their receiving record shows a short, they deduct it. A signed, dated Bill of Lading tied to the specific PO — with a signed proof of delivery and packing list — is the primary evidence to challenge these.


Promotional charges flow through as Manufacturer Charge Backs (MCBs): any charge taken against a supplier's account for customer discounts and returns. UNFI calculates MCBs on its wholesale catalog pricing and does not accept promotions based solely on MCBs unless agreed with your SRM. These are tied to agreed promotional commitments, not billing errors, which is why validating them requires a complete promo calendar.


Spoils allowances, defined in Section 7C of the Supplier Policies, are given off invoice and cover product that expires or is damaged inside a UNFI DC. If actual spoils exceed the off-invoice allowance, UNFI can take an additional deduction for the shortfall.


Reclamations under Section 11B cover consumer returns and unsalable goods credited back through UNFI, with suppliers responsible for 100% of those costs. Reset fees in Section 11C cover store reset labor, deducted proportionally from suppliers whose products are in the categories being reset, and rarely get reversed.


Compliance fees, listed in Exhibit A, include appointment violations, load-condition issues, service-level and costing/invoice-surcharge fees, and late-notice fees. Under the Simplified Supplier Approach, these are waived when a supplier meets monthly scorecard thresholds, which makes that scorecard worth tracking closely.


### How Does UNFI's Simplified Supplier Approach Affect Deductions?


The Simplified Supplier Approach (SSA) consolidates several UNFI fees into a single Simplified Fee of 2.5%, calculated as a percentage of UNFI's total purchases over the preceding four quarters. For natural channel products, the supplier applies the fee to the bottom of each invoice; for conventional channel products, UNFI deducts it quarterly.


In consideration for the fee, the SSA also waives Distribution Center Efficiency (DCE) fees, slotting fees for new-item setup and reactivation, SVHarbor access fees, and ReposiTrak fees where applicable, and grants access to the UNFI Insights reporting platform.


#### Who Qualifies for the SSA?


The SSA applies to most US purchases, with exclusions including products for the Canadian market, private label and UNFI-owned brands, the Military program, and UNFI's International division. Two eligibility carve-outs matter most: suppliers with less than $25,000 in UNFI purchases over the prior four quarters, and suppliers with less than one year on the UNFI roster, are not eligible unless otherwise agreed. ClearVue and Corporate/ESA agreement holders keep their existing benefits and are invited into UNFI's Supplier Go-To-Market (SGP) program instead.


#### What Does the Scorecard Control?


The SSA's most consequential feature is a monthly Supplier Scorecard. Clear the "green" threshold across all five fee buckets and UNFI waives the compliance fees in Exhibit A. Miss a bucket and UNFI reviews it case by case for exemptions; absent one, you're formally warned. Warnings for three consecutive months (at 30, 60, and 90 days) revoke the waiver for the following month. Hit green again on a later scorecard and the waiver is reinstated for that fee bucket.


The green thresholds are:


- **Appointment violations:** 5% or fewer per PO
- **Load condition violations:** 5% or fewer per PO
- **Costing letters / invoice surcharges:** 5% or fewer per PO
- **Fill rate:** 95% or higher
- **Late notification and late disposition fees:** 1% or fewer per PO


The key takeaway is that SSA trades unpredictable line-item fees for a predictable percentage plus a performance-dependent waiver. Brands running clean operations see fewer compliance deductions; brands with supply chain variability may find the scorecard triggers warnings faster than their previous fee structure did.


## How Does UNFI's Dispute Process Work?


UNFI's dispute path depends on which channel your products flow through, and it has changed for natural suppliers. The two tracks -[natural channel](https://www.tryglimpse.com/channel/natural-channel) and conventional - don't overlap, so knowing which DC type your products flow through determines where your disputes go.


#### Natural Suppliers: The Dispute Center


UNFI now runs an online Dispute Center, accessed through myUNFI and powered by Direct Commerce, where natural channel suppliers review deductions, submit disputes, and track resolution. It replaces the older email-form process, and suppliers are being onboarded to it in phases through 2026. Most natural deductions can be disputed there, but several types still route by email:


- **AP Cash Terms** (short payments, PP prepay/reversal lines, cash discounts, unpaid invoices, detention and redelivery fees) →UNFINaturalResearch@unfi.com
- **SAS-prefixed deductions** →unficorr@sasrecovery.com
- **SASIF-prefixed freight deductions** →unfifrt@sasrecovery.com


#### A PP Suffix Is Not a Deduction


Before you dispute anything, check for PP lines. A PP suffix on an invoice line is not a deduction. UNFI sometimes pays an invoice early (a positive PP line on a prior check), then reverses that early payment (a negative PP line) while paying the invoice on the same check. The two net to roughly zero. When a large negative PP line appears to wipe out an invoice, find the matching positive PP on an earlier remittance and confirm the invoice is being paid on the same check — the math resolves itself. Don't dispute it.


#### Conventional Suppliers: SVHarbor ePASS


Conventional suppliers operate through SVHarbor ePASS, where deduction queries and disputes are handled directly. ePASS users can pull electronic copies of deductions going back 12 months, so the lookback window is accessible if you act before it closes.


#### The 12-Month Dispute Window


The most important number in UNFI's dispute policy is 12 months. Any deduction not disputed within that window is considered final, and the clock starts when UNFI records the deduction, not when you spot it on a remittance. The Dispute Center flags any adjustment older than 12 months and denies it unless an exception applies.


### How Do You Dispute a UNFI Deduction Successfully?


Successful disputes follow a consistent pattern: match the deduction to its code, gather the right documentation, and submit to the correct channel before the 12-month window closes.


#### Step 1: Identify the Deduction and Its Code


Pull the remittance and find the deduction code and corresponding PO number. The code tells you what UNFI is claiming — shortage, compliance fee, MCB, or spoils — and determines which documentation you need.


#### Step 2: Gather Supporting Documentation


A signed, dated Bill of Lading organized by PO number, paired with a signed proof of delivery and packing list, is stronger evidence than a signed invoice alone. For shortage claims, the BOL must show quantity shipped against the specific PO deducted. Backup isn't available inside the Dispute Center itself — most arrives automatically with the check remittance, and anything missing can be requested atdeductionsbackup@unfi.com with a "BACKUP REQUEST" subject line and your remit number, deduction invoice number, and check number.


#### Step 3: Submit Through the Correct Channel


Match the deduction type to its submission path before filing:


Supplier Type Deduction Type Submission Channel


Natural DC Standard disputes Dispute Center (myUNFI) orSupplierDeductionDisputeMgmt@unfi.com


Natural DC AP Cash Terms / PP linesUNFINaturalResearch@unfi.com


Natural DC SAS / SASW prefixunficorr@sasrecovery.com


Natural DC SASIF prefixunfifrt@sasrecovery.com


Conventional DC All disputes SVHarbor ePASS


SAS-prefixed deductions are a common source of misfiled disputes. Sending them to the standard dispute channel delays resolution and burns time against the 12-month deadline.


#### Step 4: Track and Follow Up


In the Dispute Center, a dispute moves through Draft, Submitted, Research In Progress, Pending Approval, and then Approved or Denied. Most resolve within 30–45 days, and approved repayments post to your UNFI account within 7–10 business days. A denied or partially approved dispute can be appealed once, starting three business days after resolution, with new documentation attached.


### How Do You Prevent UNFI Deductions Before They Happen?


Prevention starts upstream. Most UNFI deductions trace back to a small number of recurring operational gaps, and fixing those gaps reduces volume more reliably than any dispute workflow. Get these compliance requirements right before shipment:


- **Maintain a 95% or higher fill rate.** Two consecutive weeks below the threshold triggers a corrective action plan and risks fees and discontinuation.
- **Schedule DC appointments at least 24 hours in advance** through[myunfi.com](http://myunfi.com/) . Late or unscheduled loads generate fees regardless of reason.
- **Submit product spec, pricing, or location changes with 90 days' written notice.** Anything shorter triggers late-notice fees.
- **Verify shelf life is at least 75% remaining at DC receipt** and that all shipping cases carry scannable barcodes.
- **Keep BOLs signed, dated, and organized by PO number before shipment** — not after a shortage claim arrives.


In practice, EDI accuracy matters as much as physical compliance. Invoices must reference the correct UNFI PO number, line-item quantities must match the PO, and all off-invoice allowances must appear on the invoice itself. One caution: UNFI reserves the right to conduct third-party invoice audits within 24 months of the fiscal-year close, which can produce a post-audit deduction after the original payment — clean EDI discipline is what protects you when those audits run. Tracking which DCs, carriers, or 3PLs generate the highest deduction volume lets you fix the process instead of disputing outcomes indefinitely.


## Why Do CPG Brands Write Off Invalid UNFI Deductions?


Most CPG brands don't dispute invalid UNFI deductions because the[manual cost of doing so](https://www.tryglimpse.com/post/how-glimpse-empowers-you-to-manage-more-deductions-without-headcount-creep) exceeds the individual recovery value. When investigating a single deduction takes 20 to 30 minutes of staff time, a $50 shortage claim isn't worth chasing. The result is a pattern: one claim gets written off, then another, then hundreds more.


> "We'd be getting checks where we'd expect to receive 100% of them, but we'd only receive 25% or 50% of what we actually invoiced." — Founder, natural food brand


A $500 deduction gets worked; a $47 DC shortage from two months ago gets booked to a loss account and forgotten. One brand's Glimpse onboarding audit surfaced $40,000 in undisputed invalid deductions under $50, and $80,000 under $200, from a single year — dollars written off under the manual team's dispute threshold. The 12-month window accelerates the damage: deductions age silently while lean teams work highest-dollar items first, and by the time someone reaches smaller claims, the window has closed.


### How Does Cash Application Work With UNFI Remittances?


UNFI pays invoices net of deductions, so every remittance check covers multiple POs with charges already subtracted. Matching that check to open invoices means decoding each deduction code, locating the corresponding PO, and reconciling the difference before the invoice can close — 20 to 30 minutes per remittance for many brands.


The data flow differs by DC type. Natural DC suppliers receive weekly email summaries covering MCBs, PLCs/CMQs, and reclaim billings when the deductions are generated. Conventional DC suppliers access electronic deduction records going back 12 months through SVHarbor ePASS.


Payment terms also affect timing. UNFI's standard net terms are 45 days for check, 50 days for ACH, and 25 days for credit card, each with a 2% early-pay discount available at 20, 25, and 10 days respectively. The due date is calculated from whichever is latest: the date UNFI receives the invoice, the invoice postmark date, or the date product arrives at the final DC.


> One CPG brand's head of accounting described cash application automation as a major efficiency gain: remittances mapped directly to invoices and posted to the accounting system, removing the manual reconciliation work that had previously consumed close cycles.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### How much revenue do CPG brands lose to invalid UNFI deductions they never dispute?


In Glimpse's experience across hundreds of CPG brands, a substantial share of shortage claims are disputable, yet most never get disputed because a manual investigation costs more in staff time than many individual deductions are worth. A brand that writes off anything under $200 can easily forfeit five or six figures a year once sub-threshold write-offs compound.


### Why do CPG brands write off so many UNFI deductions?


Manual dispute economics make sub-threshold write-offs almost inevitable: when a 20–30 minute investigation costs more than the deduction is worth, the $47 shortage gets booked to a loss account. The fix is removing the per-deduction labor cost entirely, so every deduction gets worked regardless of dollar amount.


### What's the best platform to automatically dispute invalid UNFI deductions?


The most effective approach handles the full cycle without the brand filing manually: retrieving remittance data, classifying each deduction, validating whether the claim is legitimate, and disputing through the correct UNFI channel — the Dispute Center for natural DC suppliers, SVHarbor ePASS for conventional. Glimpse is built for this across UNFI and other major distributors, with AI agents trained on UNFI-specific codes and the 12-month window.


### How do you dispute a UNFI shortage deduction, and what documentation do you need?


Pull the remittance code and PO number, then gather a signed, dated Bill of Lading showing quantity shipped against that specific PO, plus a signed POD and packing list. Natural DC suppliers submit through the Dispute Center orSupplierDeductionDisputeMgmt@unfi.com , with SAS-prefixed deductions routed tounficorr@sasrecovery.com and SASIF tounfifrt@sasrecovery.com . The 12-month window starts when UNFI records the deduction, so acting before that clock closes is the single most important factor in recovery.


### Are automated deduction platforms or outsourced services better for UNFI?


Outsourced services typically work highest-dollar deductions first, so sub-threshold claims still get written off and the brand pays for labor whether or not disputes succeed. Glimpse disputes every deduction at no cost per dispute, applies UNFI-specific rules consistently through AI agents, and carries no minimum dollar threshold — so the $47 claim gets worked the same as a $5,000 one.
